transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… my wife wanted me to come in. She thinks I’m not eating enough. I don’t know, I just don’t feel I need much—usually coffee and toast in the morning, maybe some soup or vegetables later. Big meals just feel a bit unnecessary at my age.
How old are you?
Seventy-eight.
Have you lost weight recently?
A bit, I suppose. My doctor says the number’s gotten too low… but I don’t really see it that way. Being lighter makes it easier for me to get around the garden and keep up with my walks.
Are you trying to lose weight?

I wouldn’t say I’m trying to lose weight, exactly… but when my wife puts butter on things or gives me a full plate, I do get uneasy. I suppose I worry I’ll start putting it back on and lose the control I’ve kept.
Do you think you would eat more if you weren't worried about gaining weight?

Maybe… yes. If I didn’t get so uneasy about putting weight back on, I suppose I might manage more. It’s just when there’s butter on things, or a full plate, I start feeling like I’m losing the bit of control I’ve kept.
Is your unease about eating more due to a fear of gaining weight?
Yes… I suppose that’s part of it. When there’s butter on things, or my wife gives me a full plate, I get nervous I’ll start putting weight back on… and lose the control I’ve had.
Do you think you are at a healthy weight now?

I think so, yes. I don’t really see why everyone’s making such a fuss. I’m older now, and older people don’t eat as much, do they? I’m still getting my chores done, still managing my tours… so it doesn’t seem that unhealthy to me.
Do you think you look too fat even when others say you are too thin?

I wouldn’t say too fat, exactly… but if I catch my stomach looking a bit rounded in the mirror, I don’t like it. Makes me feel I’ve let myself get sloppy. And if my belt’s a notch looser, well… that feels better, like I’ve done something right.
Do you think you look too thin even when you're at a weight that others consider healthy for you?

I don’t know if I’d say I look too thin. I just… if my belt feels a notch looser, it feels like I’ve done right by myself. But if my stomach looks even a little rounded in the mirror, I feel sloppy. Disappointed, I suppose.
Do you think your weight or body shape is the reason you feel uneasy about eating more?
I suppose… yes, a bit. When my wife puts butter on things, or gives me a full plate, I get uneasy. I don’t want to start putting weight back on and lose the control I’ve kept.
Do you think you would eat more if you didn't worry about how your body looks?

Maybe… yes. It’s hard to say. I do notice those things — if my belt’s a bit looser, I feel I’ve done something right. But if my stomach looks even a little rounded, I feel… sloppy, disappointed. So I suppose that does hold me back.
Do you think your body looks the way you think it should?
Not really, I suppose. I feel better when my belt’s a little looser, like I’m doing something right. But if I see any roundness in my stomach… I don’t like it. Makes me feel sloppy.
Do you think your eating habits are affected by how you perceive your body shape?

Yes… I think it is. If my belt feels a notch looser, I feel like I’ve done right by myself. But if I catch my stomach looking even a little rounded in the mirror, I feel… sloppy. Disappointed, I suppose.
Do you think your eating habits would change if you had a different perception of your body shape?

I suppose it might, yes. If I didn’t see my stomach that way… if I didn’t feel bad when it looks a bit rounded, maybe I wouldn’t hold back so much. I do tend to feel better when my belt’s looser, like I’ve done something right.
Is your fear of gaining weight the main reason you limit your food intake?
Yes… I suppose it is. When my wife puts butter on things, or gives me a full plate, I get nervous. Like I’ll start putting weight back on and lose the control I’ve been trying to keep.
Do you think your fear of gaining weight is because you believe you would look unacceptably fat at a higher weight?
Yes… I think that’s part of it. If my stomach looks even a little rounded, I feel… sloppy, I suppose. Like I’ve let myself go. But if my belt’s a bit looser, I feel I’ve done something right.
Do you think you would still be afraid of gaining weight if you didn't care about how your body looks?

I think… maybe, yes. Even if it wasn’t about how I looked, I’d still get nervous when my wife puts butter on things or gives me a full plate. It feels like I’d start putting weight back on and lose the control I’ve been trying to keep.
Do you think your fear of gaining weight is mostly because of how you think you would look at a higher weight?
Mostly, yes. I don’t like saying it, but if I see my stomach looking even a little rounded, I feel… disappointed in myself. And if my belt’s looser, I feel like I’ve done something right.
Is your fear of gaining weight mostly about how it would make you feel about your body?
Yes… I suppose it is. When my belt feels a bit looser, I feel like I’ve done right by myself. But if I catch my stomach looking rounded at all, I just feel… sloppy. Disappointed.
Do you think your weight is the only thing that determines how you feel about your body?

Not the only thing, I suppose… but it weighs on it a lot. If my belt feels a notch looser, I feel like I’ve done right by myself. If my stomach looks even a little rounded in the mirror, I feel… sloppy. Disappointed.
